reasoning: The package is a standard AUR -bin package that downloads prebuilt binaries from the official GitHub releases (https://github.com/letstri/druk) with SHA256 checksum verification. The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable definitions and a minimal package() function that installs the binary to /usr/bin/druk. No suspicious commands, obfuscation, or unexpected network operations are present. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully reviewed both PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO and correctly identified the package as safe. The qwen3-235b model's inconclusive verdict was due to an API error on .SRCINFO, not a security concern—its PKGBUILD review was also safe. The openrouter/free report is advisory-only and also failed due to an API error.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool errors, not security findings. qwen3-235b encountered an HTTP 400 error when reviewing .SRCINFO, resulting in an inconclusive verdict despite correctly assessing PKGBUILD as safe. openrouter/free (advisory-only) had an empty LLM response error. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed both files and found them safe. When tools function correctly, they consistently identify this as a safe, standard -bin package.
coverage_issues: openrouter/free: LLM response error prevented PKGBUILD review (advisory-only report)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, empty responses) should be clearly distinguished from security-based inconclusive verdicts in the final result

When one model successfully completes a full review and finds no issues, while other models' inconclusive verdicts are due to tool errors rather than security concerns, the complete safe verdict should prevail
The audit system should track whether inconclusive results are due to missing file coverage vs. genuine security uncertainty
